noAccess.title: No access to workspaces
noAccess.text: Workspaces, GPU time and JupyterHub come with projects. For most people a personal project from a budget that is approved at once is enough.

envs.title: GPU environments
envs.intro: An environment is built from a public Git repository: requirements.txt, environment.yml and similar files decide what is installed (repo2docker). Every environment comes with JupyterLab and VS Code. On start, the repository is placed in the own home under ~/projekte.
envs.name: Name
envs.addHint: Public repositories on GitHub and GitLab are allowed. If this version already exists as a built environment, it can be started at once; otherwise it is built (usually 2–10 minutes). A Dockerfile of its own is allowed if it builds on a platform image from registry.gpu.services.dhbw.cloud/platform/.
envs.startCpuHint: Start a server without GPU (up to 4 CPU cores, 8 GB RAM)
envs.startGpuHint: Start a server with a GPU; waits until a GPU is free and counts against the GPU quota
envs.deleteMessage: “{{name}}” disappears from the list. Files in the home stay, running servers keep running.
envs.startedCpu: The server is starting and is usually ready within a minute.
envs.startedGpu: The server starts as soon as a GPU is free. If all are busy, it waits in the queue.
envs.startedHome: The repository is in the home under <1>~/projekte</1>; own changes are kept at the next start.
envs.logNone: No build log (the environment had been built before, or the build is older than a day).
envs.projectHint: The server runs in this project and counts against its limits.

servers.title: Running servers
servers.intro: All own servers in JupyterHub, including those started there directly. Idle servers end by themselves: without GPU after 2 hours, with GPU after 30 minutes.
servers.name: Server
servers.stopMessage: “{{name}}” is stopped. Files in the home stay, unsaved changes in open notebooks are lost.

usage.title: Usage
usage.hint: What workspaces reserved from {{from}} to {{to}}: server hours, vCPU, RAM and GPU hours, home size. Collected every minute; today is not complete yet.
usage.csvHint: The grouping shown as CSV, with the measured values.
usage.explain: What is charged is the reservation (requested cores and memory), as with flavors in OpenStack. “CPU used” relates the measured use to it. Home GB-days: space used, measured hourly, the day's largest value counts; a project's storage is listed as “Projektspeicher”.

projects.freeImagesHint: Any image, with or without a GPU, with home directory and project folder. It runs without root rights and must contain jupyterhub-singleuser.
projects.limits: Limits per person (at the same time)
projects.limitsHint: Counted is what one person runs in this project at the same time. 0 means no limit – except for GPUs, where 0 means no GPU.
projects.budgetsHint: Tighter limits within the project quotas, e.g. at most 40 vCPU hours per person in 7 days, so nobody uses up the quota alone. Windows in calendar days: “today”, 7 or 30 days including today, “total” since the project was created. Once a limit is reached, no server starts and running servers end within 5 minutes (the home stays).
projects.profilesHint: What members can choose when starting a server in JupyterHub. The platform sets the list; GPU types count against the project's GPU quotas.

storage.title: Storage (admins)
storage.hint: Workspace storage on JuiceFS: one volume per project with storage, plus homes from before the projects. Measured hourly.
storage.ofNode: of the node's {{total}} GB RAM · peak {{peak}} GB
storage.noReport: No measurement since the AI service last restarted; the next comes on the hour.
storage.explain: A project's limit is its workspace storage from the budget tree; a full volume refuses further writes. The metadata grow with the number of files (roughly 1 GB RAM per 2–3 million files); when RAM runs short, JuiceFS stops.
